title: Enbridge franchise agreement and gas fee advocacy
subtitle: Committee also received the Blue Box transition update, recognized staff achievements, and heard budget town hall announcements.
overview: The committee spent most of the afternoon on the municipal franchise agreement with Enbridge Gas. It voted down staff's recommendation to approve a new 20-year agreement and ask the Ontario Energy Board to approve it without a vote of electors {{vote:m6}}. It received the staff report for information {{vote:m5}}. A closed session earlier in the day on the same item produced no decisions or staff direction.

The committee then recommended a package of advocacy motions {{vote:m10}}. It asks the province to let municipalities charge fees to for-profit gas utilities for use of public property. It directs staff to negotiate a franchise agreement that allows such fees if the rules change, protects the city from relocation costs, and keeps new charges off Guelph gas customers. It also supports Bill 219 in principle. Because this was a Committee of the Whole meeting, these are recommendations for Council to consider later.

Residents should know the city cannot currently charge these fees under provincial rules. Staff said the existing agreement continues if a new one is not approved. The committee also received the Blue Box transition update {{vote:m11}}. Guelph moves to the provincial producer-funded system on January 1, 2025.

decisions.detail: The committee received the Enbridge franchise agreement report for information, after an amendment adding those words so the public understands what receipt means.
The committee defeated the staff clauses to approve the form of franchise agreement, submit it to the Ontario Energy Board, and seek an order that elector assent is not needed {{vote:m6}}.
The committee amended the advocacy motion so staff negotiate the franchise agreement to the satisfaction of the Deputy CAO of Infrastructure, Development and Environment {{vote:m8}}.
The committee amended the advocacy motion so the city supports Bill 219, the "No Free Ride for Fossil Fuels Act, 2024", in principle rather than outright {{vote:m9}}.

The committee recommended that Council ask the province to allow fees on gas utilities, direct staff to negotiate a franchise agreement with fee, relocation-cost and customer-protection terms, support Bill 219 in principle, and circulate the motions to provincial and municipal bodies {{vote:m10}}.
The committee received the Blue Box Transition Status Update report {{vote:m11}}.

debate: Delegates urged the committee not to sign a 20-year agreement. They argued that Enbridge pays little for its use of public land and that fees could fund city programs, and some linked the issue to climate goals and the proposed budget cuts to environmental programs. Several young delegates spoke about their future. One delegate asked for a shorter term or a deferral.

Some councillors voted against the staff recommendation to send a signal to the province. They noted that the city cannot charge these fees now and that the agreement would likely be imposed anyway. Others supported the staff recommendation, citing the regulatory reality and the staff time that further work would take.

One councillor argued that new fees on Enbridge would reach ratepayers through later Energy Board rate reviews. The councillor said this would raise gas bills and affect affordability. Others said making the cost visible supports the shift away from fossil fuels.

Staff said there is no budget line item paying Enbridge and that Enbridge pays property tax and permit and inspection fees. Staff said the term "subsidy" is loaded. Staff also said the current agreement continues if Council does not approve the new one, and that either party can apply to the Energy Board.

On the amendment adding "in principle" to Bill 219 support, one councillor said the bill was new and had not been debated, and raised concerns about how rates would be negotiated. Opponents said the one-page bill was already public and they supported it in full. On Blue Box, councillors asked about public communications, and staff described a multi-pronged plan with customer service support.
